idiom_name: HashMap<TypeId, Arc<dyn Any + Send + Sync>> with downcast::<T>()
implementation_notes: Rust has neither reflection nor a container, so the classic locator must be built from std::any: TypeId::of::<T>() as the key, Arc<dyn Trait> (or Box<dyn Any + Send + Sync>) as the erased slot, and downcast_ref/downcast::<T>() for checked retrieval - services are shared, so Arc is handed out by clone. The registry itself should be a value passed down from main; a process-wide one lives behind OnceLock for one-time initialisation, or RwLock when registrations continue after startup. When the service set is fixed, a struct with typed fields beats the TypeId map because the compiler then checks the graph.
pitfalls: TypeId erases the link between a service and its consumer: a forgotten insert() is an Option::None at run time that the compiler could never have caught.
OnceLock initialises exactly once, so tests needing different graphs in one process must use their own Registry value rather than the global.

Never call a service while holding the registry lock: clone the Arc under the lock and release it, or a service that resolves another service re-enters the lock and deadlocks (std locks are not reentrant).

variants.name: Distributed registration with the inventory crate
variants.implementation_notes: When contributions must arrive from many source files without a central list, inventory turns the registry into a link-time collection: the plugin type is declared with inventory::collect!, each contributor calls inventory::submit!, and the host iterates inventory::iter::<T>. That is how Rust libraries collect command-line flags, migrations, or test cases while avoiding a merge-conflict-prone central table; the cost is that registration happens before main, so nothing may depend on the registry during static initialisation, and iteration order is unspecified. Use linkme instead when life-before-main is unacceptable.
pitfalls: Registration runs before main, so a partially initialised program can observe a partial registry; on platforms without static initialisers nothing is registered at all and the collection is silently empty.
inventory::iter order is unspecified - never let migrations, hooks or plugins depend on submission order.
The collected statics must be 'static and constructible in a const context, which rules out services that need configuration or fallible construction.
